properties.title: Gazprom Under Investigation for Major Gasoline Sales Cuts Amid Soaring Prices
properties.summary: Gazprom is facing a formal investigation by Russia's Federal Anti-Monopoly Service for significantly reducing gasoline sales of Ai-92 and Ai-95 at the St Petersburg commodity exchange, with cuts of 74% and 50% from its Surgut plant. This investigation underscores the government's response to soaring gasoline prices and aims to address concerns over fuel supply during high-demand periods, marking a pivotal moment in regulatory oversight of the energy sector.

properties.title: FAS Investigates Gazprom Over Gasoline Sales Drop
properties.summary: The Federal Anti-Monopoly Service of Russia has initiated an investigation into Gazprom due to a significant drop in gasoline sales, which the regulator deems unacceptable amid seasonal demand. This inquiry raises concerns about potential violations of antimonopoly laws by the company.

properties.subcategory: Anti-Competitive Practices, Legal And Investigative Exposure
properties.title: Orlen Faces $290 Million Liability After Arbitration Ruling on Gazprom Gas Prices
properties.summary: Orlen faces a significant financial blow following an arbitration tribunal's ruling that allows Gazprom to retroactively charge higher gas prices, potentially costing the company nearly $290 million. This ruling pertains to gas prices from 2017 to 2022 and is compounded by existing sanctions that prevent Orlen from making payments to Gazprom. The tribunal is also set to review additional claims regarding gas prices for 2021 and 2022, alongside Gazprom's suspension of gas supplies to Poland, raising concerns about the broader implications for energy security in the region.

properties.title: Gazprom Faces $7 Billion Losses and Asset Expropriation Amid European Gas Crisis
properties.summary: In a significant turn of events, Gazprom is facing nearly $7 billion in financial losses in 2023, primarily due to a drastic decline in gas sales to Europe amid the ongoing Ukraine conflict. The company has announced its withdrawal from Germany following a decree from President Putin mandating gas payments in rubles, which Germany has rejected, leading to potential asset expropriation by the German government. Additionally, the nationalization of Gazprom's former subsidiary, Sefe, aims to secure gas supplies and reduce Russian influence, while discussions of tax relief for Gazprom signal a shift towards increasing gas exports to Asia, particularly China.

properties.subcategory: Anti-Competitive Practices, Legal And Investigative Exposure
properties.title: Gazprom Granted Right to Retroactively Charge Higher Gas Prices to Poland
properties.summary: A recent arbitration ruling in Stockholm has granted Gazprom the right to retroactively charge higher prices for gas supplied to Poland, potentially costing Orlen nearly $300 million. This decision adds to the ongoing legal disputes between Gazprom and its clients, with further claims anticipated from both parties.

properties.title: Gazprom Demands €16 Billion from Slovakia Amid EU's Push to End Russian Gas Imports
properties.summary: Gazprom is demanding €16 billion from Slovakia for terminating a long-term gas contract, following Slovakia's declaration of force majeure by its state-owned gas importer, SPP. This demand underscores the financial risks Slovakia faces as it aligns with the EU's strategy to phase out Russian gas imports by 2027, despite the contract's validity until 2034.

properties.title: ICC Tribunal Rules Against Gazprom in CEZ Gas Supply Dispute, Mandates International Arbitration
properties.summary: In a pivotal legal ruling, an ICC tribunal has barred Gazprom from pursuing its legal claims against CEZ in Russian courts, mandating that the dispute over a $44 million gas supply failure be resolved through international arbitration. This decision underscores the growing significance of international legal frameworks in energy disputes, particularly in the context of heightened geopolitical tensions following Russia's invasion of Ukraine.

properties.title: ICC Tribunal Rules Against Gazprom in CEZ Dispute
properties.summary: An ICC tribunal has ruled that Gazprom must cease its legal actions against CEZ in Russian courts, mandating that any disputes be settled through ICC arbitration. This decision follows CEZ's request for an interim measure, highlighting a significant shift in the legal landscape surrounding the case.

In August 2020, the Office of Competition and Consumer Protection of Poland fined Gazprom PAO almost PLN 213 million. The company failed to provide information relevant to the investigation into the construction of Nord Stream 2. Charges had been brought against Gazprom PAO as well as Engie SA, Uniper, OMV AG, Royal Dutch Shell plc and Wintershall Dea GmbH. The companies concluded contracts for the construction of the gas pipeline project without the required approval from the Polish authority.

In October 2020, the Office of Competition and Consumer Protection of Poland imposed a fine of PLN 29,075,726,808 on Gazprom PAO. Engie SA, Uniper, OMV AG, Royal Dutch Shell plc and Wintershall Dea GmbH were fined as well. Gazprom and the other five companies were financial investors in the gas pipeline system Nord Stream 2.
